body.html: Yala Grand Palace Hotel is a 109-room hotel on Chalermchai Road in Sateng, central Yala. It is a 7-storey building with a lift, positioned as a city hotel that leans on location and convenience rather than luxury. With its large room count and central setting, it suits business travellers, people working in town, visitors exploring Yala city, and families wanting an affordable base near the mall and market.

The thing reviews mention first is the friendly, attentive staff. Voices from real guest reviews describe a warm front desk that smiles and helps with things easily. Another common compliment is the large free car park, with plenty of space for both cars and motorbikes, a genuine plus if you drive yourself or rent a vehicle to explore the three southern provinces. The overall feel is a plain but practical city hotel that does the job.
"Decent-sized room, lovely helpful staff, lots of parking, and an easy walk to the mall and market in town. Great value for a one-night stop."

On the rooms, most reviews say they are roomy enough, clean enough and comfortable for the price. Rooms have air-conditioning, a refrigerator, a flat-screen TV, hot water and the basics. There are twin rooms, double rooms and larger VIP rooms, some decorated to their own theme. The thing to understand is that the building and furnishings are showing their age, and a few reviews note dated decor and rooms that vary in condition, which is normal for a city hotel at this price. Looking at photos of each room type and picking a more recently renovated one helps.

On amenities, there is an on-site restaurant with halal options, handy for travellers who eat halal. There are meeting rooms for seminars and events, which makes it popular for functions in Yala. Wi-Fi is free throughout and there is a staffed front desk. To be clear-eyed, there is no swimming pool, and breakfast depends on the rate you book — some don't include it, so check at booking. If you prefer to eat out, no problem: restaurants, cafes and the town market are all within easy reach.

Worth knowing before you book: this is a city hotel, and the area is fairly busy with traffic during the day. Road-facing rooms may pick up some outside noise, so asking for a higher floor or an inward-facing room helps. Some reviews mention weak water pressure and slow hot water in certain rooms, plus a lift that can be slow at busy times, all typical of an older city hotel. Overall it remains a practical stay at a price that is genuinely cheap for a room this size in the town centre.

In short, Yala Grand Palace Hotel suits travellers who value a central location, low price and parking over luxury or resort-style facilities. Its strengths are clear: the heart of Yala, a walk to the mall and market, close to the train station, free parking and halal food. But if you want a pool, a sleek new room or a boutique feel, compare it against other hotels in town. For a Yala trip built around exploring the city, business, or an overnight stop before driving on to Betong, this is a tidy, wallet-friendly base.

A tip from reading the reviews: pick a more recently renovated room and ask for a higher inward-facing floor for better condition and quieter nights. If you drive, the free parking is genuinely handy, and you can ask the hotel restaurant about halal options. Yala and Betong fill up on Thai long weekends and festivals, so rooms go fast; reserve ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans are not yet firm.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Yala Grand Palace Hotel

faq.q: Where is Yala Grand Palace Hotel, and what is within walking distance?
faq.a: It sits at 82-84 Chalermchai Road, Sateng, Mueang Yala, in the city centre. The mall and market in town are about a 10-minute walk, Yala train station is about 0.8 km away and Yala Rajabhat University about 1.5 km. Restaurants, cafes and town sights are all within easy reach.

faq.q: What is the starting price, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start around THB 650/night for a standard twin and about THB 800 for a double. There are larger Deluxe rooms and themed VIP rooms for families at around THB 1,200. Rates vary by season and holidays, so always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does it have a swimming pool and halal food?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool, but there is an on-site restaurant with halal options, convenient for travellers who eat halal. Breakfast depends on the rate you book — some don't include it, so check at booking. Restaurants and the town market are also within easy walking distance.

faq.q: Who is Yala Grand Palace Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits business travellers, people attending meetings, visitors exploring Yala city and those stopping overnight before Betong who value a central location, low price and parking. There is free parking and there are meeting rooms. If you want a pool, a new room or a boutique feel, compare it with other options in town.

faq.q: Is there anything to know before staying?
faq.a: Know that the building is ageing and room condition varies — look at photos and ask for a more recently renovated room. The central area has traffic and road-facing rooms catch some noise, so request a higher inward-facing floor. Some rooms have weak water pressure and slow hot water, and the lift can be slow at busy times. Yala and Betong fill up on Thai long weekends, so book ahead.
